source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide how to answer a large real-world feasibility question by choosing assumptions, converting units, calculating, and comparing with the target.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Unit conversion is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide how to answer a large real-world feasibility question by' is answered as unit conversion rather than assumption.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Unit conversion is what produces assumption, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide how to answer a large real-world feasibility.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: assumption is settled by running 'Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or small only after': The same number can feel large in one context and ordinary in another; one lakh rice — on the item about Decide how to answer a large real-world feasibility.

mx.name: operation_confusion
mx.teacher_note: Assumption is found by dividing the given values instead of multiplying, giving 49 as the reported result — on the item about Decide how to answer a large real-world feasibility.

intelligence.enrichment: For large-number situations, state or use reasonable assumptions, convert quantities to compatible units, calculate by multiplication or division, and compare the result with the target to decide whether it is possible or how long it takes.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_07/ch_101. The student must decide: Decide how to answer a large real-world feasibility question by choosing assumptions, converting units, calculating, and comparing with the target. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
